header_sentences: See Merum, and Must; and also see Drunk, Strong drink, Vine, Vineyard, and Vintage.

contexts.text: (Noah) drank of the wine () = that he wanted to investigate (by reasonings) the things of faith. Explained.

Vineyard, or vine = the Spiritual Church... the grapes... = charity... and the wine = the derivative faith, and all things that are of faith; thus... the wine = the Spiritual of that Church. Illustrated.

Wine () = the Spiritual from the Celestial; the blood of grapes = the Celestial relatively to Spiritual Churches; thus grapes = charity itself; and wine = faith itself. ( = the Divine good and Divine truth of the Natural. AC 3300:2.) See AC 5117:8.
As grapes = charity, so wine = the derivative faith; for wine is from grapes.
Not to tread out wine in the presses () = that there are no longer any who are in faith.
Wine () = the truths of faith.
As wine = faith in the Lord, faith... was represented by a libation of wine. Illustrated.
Wine of whoredom () = the adulterated truths of faith, of which drunkenness is predicated. ( = falsity from evil. AC 8904:5.) AR 721.
A vinous odour... comes from those who compliment one another from friendship, (so that) there is truth in the compliments. SE 1047.
(Melchizedek) brought forth bread and wine () = celestial and spiritual things and the refreshment from them. Explained.
For, in the Ancient Church, wine was a representative of all spiritual things; thus, here, of the Lord Himself...

The wine (in the Holy Supper) = all spiritual things. ( = His Divine Spiritual. AC 2830.) ( = His Divine truth. AC 3813:2.) ( = spiritual love. AC 4211.) ( = the Holy of charity and faith in Heaven. AC 4700:2.) ( = Divine spiritual love. AC 4735:2.) ( = charity. AC 6789:3.) ( = the Lord as to the truth of faith, and its reception by man. AC 10149:end.) ( = the good of faith. AC 10521.) ( = the Lord as to Divine truth; and, with the recipients, holy truth from the Lord. AR 316:2.) ( = Divine truth. TCR 238. TCR 372.) ( = the good of faith, which in its essence is truth. AE 376:26.) ( = the good of faith which in its essence is truth from good; and, in the supreme sense, the Lord as to Divine truth. AE 376:26.) ( = truth from this good, which is also the good of faith. AE 617:20.) ( = the Divine truth. AE 1082:2.)

Buy wine and milk () = the Spiritual of faith, and the Spiritual of love. ( = spiritual truth, and spiritual good. AC 2967:9.) ( = the good of faith. AC 8568:2.) ( = the truth of good, and the good of truth. AC 8976:end.) ( = spiritual good which in its essence is truth, and the good of this truth. AE 376:4.) ( = Divine truth spiritual, and Divine truth natural. AE 617:10.)
As wine and grapes... = what is spiritual, the Nazarite was forbidden to eat of them. Explained. AC 5113:17. AE 918:11, Explained.
Wines sweet [on the lees] and refined () = truths derived from (goods). (This is said in relation to the Holy Supper. TCR 708.)
Let us make our father drink wine () = that they should imbue such good with falsities. AC 2465:4.
Wine = truth. AC 4581:10. AE 475:6.
Not to drink wine with a song () = not to be instructed from the affection of truth, and not to be delighted thereby. (Compare AE 323:2.) ( = no heavenly bliss. AE 376:20.)
Instead of wine (the Angels perceive) spiritual love and the things of it, that is, of love towards the neighbour. AC 3316:3. AC 3464:2.
(Esau) brought him wine, and he drank () = the conjunction of truth afterwards. (For) wine = the truth that is from good.
(The drinking of wine, in the Ancient Church) = what is of charity towards the neighbour.
His eyes are redder than wine (or, are red with wine) () = the Divine wisdom. ( = that the Intellectual, or the internal Human, is nothing but good. AC 6379.) ( = the Divine truth. AR 316:2.)
When wine is read in the Word, or is received in the Holy Supper, the Angels think... about charity towards the neighbour...
Under Bread, see this reference.
They shall drink the wine () = to appropriate the truths of the Spiritual Church, which are of charity. ( = to be instructed and become intelligent. AE 376:6.)

He hath washed his garment in wine, and his vesture in the blood of grapes (). The Lord is here treated of; wine = spiritual good from the Divine love; and the blood of grapes the derivative celestial good. (Wine = the Divine truth. AR 316:2. AE 195:19.) (Wine and the blood of grapes = the Divine truth. AE 376:20. AE 475:12.) (See AC 6377.)

Wine is called the blood of grapes () because both = the holy truth proceeding from the Lord; but wine is predicated of the Spiritual Church; and blood of the Celestial Church. This is why wine was commanded in the Holy Supper.
See Cup.

He took the cup, and gave thanks... saying, Drink ye all of it; for this is My blood... It is said the cup, and not the wine, because wine is predicated of the Spiritual Church, and blood of the Celestial Church, although both = the holy truth proceeding from the Lord; but in the Spiritual Church, the Holy of faith from charity towards the neighbour, and in the Celestial Church, the Holy of charity from love to the Lord. (Continued. See Holy Supper.)
See Cup.
As wine inebriates and makes insane, so does falsity...
Wine (as food) corresponds to spiritual love.
See Holy Supper.
The wine of the libation = the derivative truth of faith.

He washes his garment in wine () = that His Natural is Divine truth from His Divine good... (For) wine = the good of love towards the neighbour, and the good of faith; and, in the supreme sense, the Divine truth from the Lord's Divine good. (See AE 433:4.)

That wine = love towards the neighbour, and the good of faith, is evident from... the Holy Supper, namely, that... the wine = the good of spiritual love... And so the libation of wine = the good of faith.
That wine = love towards the neighbour, and the good of faith. Illustrated.
That wine = the good of mutual love and of faith. Illustrated.
The wine () = the good of spiritual love. ( = the good and truth of faith. AC 9780:4.)

(The Samaritan) poured in oil and wine () = that he performed the works of love and charity. ( = the good of love, and the good of faith. AC 9057:2.) ( = the good of love, and the good of charity and of faith. AC 9780:6.) ( = good and its truth. NJHD 87.) ( = teaching good and truth. AR 316:4.) ( = the good and the truth that heal man. AE 375:42. AE 376:30.) ( = instructing in the good of love, and the truth of faith. AE 444:14.) AE 962:6.

That wine = the good of love and of faith, is evident from the Lord's words... I will not drink of this fruit of the vine, until the day when I shall drink it new with you... (). Explained. ( = the truth of the New Church and Heaven. TCR 708:end.)
As wine = the good of love and of faith, it = in the supreme sense, the Divine truth from the Lord's Divine good; for from this, by influx, the man who receives it has the good of love and of faith.
Wine, in the opposite sense, = falsity from evil. Illustrated.
The truth then comes forth purified, like wine, which becomes clear after fermentation.
Wine = truth from good; and, in the opposite, falsity from evil.

The first-fruits of the wine thou shalt not delay () = that as all... truths are from the Lord, they must be attributed to Him, and not to self... For wine = the truth of good, thus the truth of the good of faith.
In the Original Language, it is said... the tear of the wine... and tears are things that drop.
Thou shalt tread... the must, but not drink the wine () = to be instructed about the truths that are from good, but still not to appropriate them to one's self. AC 9277:2. AE 376:17.
The wine that is of the press = truth from good.
The wine = the internal truth of that Church.
The blood, and the wine (in the institution of the Holy Supper) = the Divine truth proceeding from the Divine good of the Lord's Divine love; and, on the other hand, the same received by man.
The wine that Noah drank, and with which he was inebriated = the falsity with which the Ancient Church became imbued in its beginning.
Wine = the truth of good.
By the drinking up of the wine (by the priests alone) is signified that they alone know Divine truth...

As in burnt-offerings... there was nothing that was pleasing in the Heavens, meat-offerings of bread, and also libations of wine, in which there was something pleasing, were also employed; for bread = all celestial good; and wine, all the truth of it.
A libation of the fourth of a hin of wine () = spiritual truth sufficient for conjunction; for wine = truth; here, spiritual truth corresponding to spiritual good from celestial. Explained.
That the libation, which was wine, = the good of faith. Illustrated.
There appeared (in the Fifth Earth) shrubs that were not vines, but which bear berries from which they prepare wine.
(References to passages on the subject of wine.)
Blood, or wine = the good of faith from the Word.
The chyle collected from things esculent and vinous.
(The bränvin of a peasant, as opposed to the noble wine of a king.)

elements.str: Vinum adustum is evidently a literal translation into Latin of the Swedish word
which means a spirituous liquor that is made from potatoes.

contexts.text: Good (then) becomes like generous wine after fermentation... But if evil conquers, good with its truth... becomes turbid and foul, like unfermented wine...
The heat (that) flows into things vinous, fragrant, etc.
Hurt not the oil and the wine () = that... the holy goods and truths which lie hidden in the Word be not violated and profaned. AE 375.
Oil = the good of love; wine, truth from this good. Illustrated. AE 375.

They do not put new wine into old bottles... (). New wine = the Divine truth of the New Testament, thus of the new Church; and the old wine = the Divine truth of the Old Testament, thus of the old Church. AE 195:15.
That wine = holy truth, is evident from its opposite sense, in which it = truth falsified and profaned. Illustrated.
He said, I have planted a vineyard; I will now drink wine even to drunkenness... out of an invisible cup... But I say unto you, Drink wine from the Word understood. Explained.

She made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication () = that by profanations of the Word, and adulterations of the good and truth of the Church, she has seduced all... Wine = truth from good; and, in the opposite sense, falsity from evil. AE 881. See AR 721. AR 758.
The wine of the anger of God mingled with unmixed () = the truth of the Word falsified, ( = falsity and the derivative evil, conjoined with falsified truths. AE 887.)
Under Vineyard, see this reference.
Wine = the Divine truth of the Word.
The wine () = their nefarious dogmas.
Wine () = truth from the good of love.
(They say) that the wine is for (the priests) lest they should be wearied out; and that water is mixed with the wine, lest they be inebriated.
The wine of the fury and anger of God () = the goods and truths of the Church, which are from the Word, profaned and adulterated; thus the evils and falsities of the Church.
(Heavenly happiness supposed to consist in feasting, with) generous and noble wines.
The trees of wine (in the garden) came next to the trees of oil.
They saw a table magnificently laid out, containing... wine jellies... and a pyramid through the middle of which there gushed out a fountain of nectareous wine...
(Wine drunk at a wedding in Heaven.)
Compared to the taste of the wine that is pressed out of the grapes.
Like grapes after the wine has been pressed out of them.
Like urine conjoined with wine of flavour.
That by the Lord's blood, and by the wine, is meant the Divine truth of His wisdom, and also all the truth of faith. General article.
That by wine is meant the like as by blood. Illustrated.
Like the fragrance in wine cellars.

The reason (the priests) did not drink wine or strong drink () was indeed from drunkenness... lest... the representations should be disturbed; for wine disturbs the life of the body and the natural life of the mind... so that the spiritual life cannot act in it becomingly...

The flame in the Habitation, the shining gold, and the aromatic odour of the incense would have been disturbed by wine, and therefore the representations would have been disturbed; besides that the odour of the wine and strong drink would have united itself with the mind... so that it could not make a distinction between what was holy and what was profane. WE 5523, Further explained.

Thus the Nazarite might (then) drink wine... because it was after he had been sanctified; for then wine could not inebriate him. It is as it is with the regenerate, to whom cupidities then do no harm, because then the cupidities are no longer excited by nature and the body... The wine is thus happiness, or heavenly joy; for it then exhilarates, and excites only the things that are of charity. WE 6880.
A disgust for wine, or intoxicating drink. See Drunk.
(Poisoned wine offered me by Dippel, the effect of which would have been to destroy the understanding.)
(The Quaker Spirit) appeared with a flask of red or dark wine, which he drank up, and so disappeared. SE 3802. SE 3803, Explained. See LJPost 59.
(Great goblets full of wine with sugar seen, with which the lascivious girls delighted themselves.)
Wine cellars seen, as representatives.

Why the Papists have separated the bread from the wine... It is not done on account of deficiency of wine, because there is wine in Italy, France, Spain, Portugal, the more interior part of Germany, and Hungary; and where wine is not produced, as in England, Holland, Sweden, Denmark, and Protestant Germany, wine does not grow - and yet it is employed in the sacrament of the Supper. The Papists could find no other reason except that the monks... should not be wearied out in their continuous labour... But it was said that it has come to pass of the Divine Providence... because good is not good if separated from truth... AE 1054:end, Explained.
A cry over the wine in the streets () = the truth of doctrine falsified, over which there is contest and indignation. (Compare AE 652:7.)
They err through wine, through strong drink they go astray... they are swallowed up by wine () = truths mixed with falsities.
Wine = the good of charity, which in its essence is truth. References.
A feast of lees, that is, of the best wines () = the appropriation of truths.
The wine is gone () = that the truth of the Church has departed. AE 376:38. AE 887:4.
In the Word... wine stands for all spiritual drink, (that is) all the truth which is communicated to man by the Lord.
Thus wine = the Divine truth proceeding from the Divine good of the Divine love; and, in relation to man, this received by him.

As by wine is meant the Divine truth nourishing the spiritual life, the Lord says... I will not drink of this product of the vine... until I shall drink it new with you. ( = the good of faith which in its essence is truth. AE 376:26.)
In the winepresses, the wine is pressed out of the grapes; and wine = the Divine truth.

That wine = spiritual good, which is the good of charity towards the neighbour and the good of faith; and... in its essence this good is truth... Hence it is that wine = truth. General article. AE 376:4, Illustrated.
Must, that is, wine () = truth.

The derivative truths are meant by the treading out of the wine in the winepresses ()... For they were wont to sing... in the winepresses when the grape was trodden into wine, on account of the representation of the delights from the truths which are signified by wine.
The truths of good that were taken away, are meant by the vintage, and the wine in the winepresses ().
Corn and wine () = all the good and truth of the Church in general. AE 750:13.
The wine of Heshbon () = natural truth.
Wine () = the truth from good from which is this heavenly delight. AE 448:8.
To drink wine out of the vessels of the Temple () = to imbibe the truths of the Church that are from the Word.
Wine () = truth falsified.
As wine = the truth of the Church which is from good... the libation of wine was commanded. Illustrated.

The product of the vine, that is, wine, which the Lord would drink new with them... = that all the Divine truth in Heaven and the Church would then be from His Divine Human. He therefore calls it new; and He also calls it the New Testament in My blood; for the Lord's blood = the like as wine.
The wine (as brought forth by Melchizedek, ) = the Divine truth, or, in application to man... the good of faith which comes from the reception of the Divine truth.

In , wine = truth; old wine, the truth of the old or Jewish Church... And that the statutes and judgments of the Jewish Church... do not accord with the truths of the Christian Church, is meant by, They do not put new wine into old bottles... And that those who have been born and brought up in the external things of the Jewish Church cannot be at once brought into the internal things of the Christian Church, is signified by, No one who drinks old wine straightway desires new; for he says, The old is more useful.

The like is signified by the water turned into wine... (which = ) the truth of the external Church, such as was that of the Jewish Church from the sense of the letter (made into) the truth of the internal Church, such as is that of the Christian Church... by opening the internal things concealed in the former.
Wine, in the opposite, = truth falsified, and also falsity. Illustrated. AE 376:37.
Smitten down with wine () = those who see falsity in place of truth... These err through wine... () = through falsities.
See Strong drink. AE 376:33.
Every bottle shall be filled with wine () = the mind of man with falsity.
To be inflamed with wine () = to hatch doctrinal things from themselves.
Heroes to drink wine () = those who aspire to great things (and who) imbibe falsities. ( = those who adulterate the truth of the Word. AE 618:3.)
The wine of the wrath of God = the falsity of evil.
Natural foods correspond to spiritual foods; as... wine to truths from good.

He washes his garment in wine () = the Lord's external or natural Human, that it is Divine truth from His Divine love; and his vesture in the blood of grapes = the Lord's internal or rational Human, that it is Divine good from His Divine love; his eyes are redder than wine = that the internal or rational Human is nothing but good...

Their wine is the poison of dragons, and the cruel gall of asps () = falsities from evil... Wine = truth from the Word; but poison of dragons, and gall of asps = the monstrous falsity that comes forth from the falsified truths of the Word. (Compare AE 519:7. AE 714:27.)
Wine, in the Word, = the good and truth of faith. AE 519:7.
Their heart shall be glad as if with wine () = the joy of such from truths.
Under Vinegar, see this reference.
His eyes red with wine = that His Intellectual was Divine truth from Divine good.
To eat flesh and drink wine () = to appropriate to one's self evil and falsity... Wine = the falsity of evil.
The vine = (the Spiritual Church) because... wine = the good of charity towards the neighbour and the good of faith.

To plant a vineyard and cultivate it, and not to drink the wine () = that although the Church is established, and the truths of doctrine are taught, still truths will not affect and perfect. Wine = the truth of doctrine.
Wine = the truth of the Church from the Word.
My cup shall run over = with the truth of doctrine from the Word; for cup here stands for wine.
To sell a girl for wine () = to falsify the goods of the Word.
As all truth is from good, as all wine is from grapes, by wine, in the Word, is signified truth from good. AE 922:6.
Wine = the truth of the Church.
The cup of the wine of the anger of Jehovah () = the falsity that is from Hell. AE 960:3.
Wine = the truth of the Word and of doctrine. AE 962:6.
Wine = spiritual truth.
Falsities from evil may be compared to wine or strong drink that induces drunkenness.
Wine = truth from Heaven; and, in the opposite, falsity from Hell.
Wine = Divine truth.
Wine, in , = truth from a celestial origin, because it is joined with oil.
Wine, in the Word, = truth, or spiritual good; for truth from a celestial origin coincides with spiritual good.
In the Second Heaven there are orchards from whose fruits drop wines.
The Mohammedans said that in Heaven they shall drink wine.
(Wines and other alcoholic drinks in the spiritual London.)
The quality of the wine according to that of the truth.
Like a vessel full of noble wine.
Goblets full of sweet, but poisoned, wine.
Wine from Heaven [was instilled] into the water in the waterpots at the wedding at Cana.
